title: Everything takes longer than planned
text: Ask people how long a task will take, then compare the estimate with reality, and a pattern emerges with depressing {{1}}: things take longer and cost more than planned. Sydney's Opera House was {{2}} to open in 1963; it opened in 1973, at fourteen times the budgeted cost. The curious thing is that experience does not {{3}} the error. Renovators who know that past projects overran remain {{4}} that this time will be different — the planning fallacy at work. Psychologists {{5}} it to a habit of mind: when we plan, we picture the steps going right, not the {{6}} that derail real projects. The imagination runs on best cases, so the forecast is really a plan — an account of how things will go if nothing goes wrong, which is to say, never. The {{7}} is not to think harder but to consult the record: how long have similar projects actually taken? Reference class forecasting, the technique that does exactly this, {{8}} the seductive details of the current plan and starts instead from the statistics of its predecessors. Cities now use it on rail projects, and forecasts improve — even though planners, being human, sometimes quietly believe their project is the exception.

gaps.explanation: 'emerges with depressing regularity' — happens reliably; regulation = a rule, regime = a government.
'was scheduled to open in 1963' — planned for that date; sketch = draw roughly, scheme = plot (usually secret).
'experience does not prevent the error' — stop it recurring; prevail = win out, and 'prevail the error' is not grammatical.
'remain convinced that this time will be different' — firmly certain; convict = find guilty, convert = change faith.

gaps.hint: ___ it to = find the origin of
gaps.explanation: 'psychologists trace it to a habit of mind' — find its source in; track suggests physical pursuit rather than origins.
'the snags that derail real projects' — hidden difficulties; snap = a sudden break, snub = an insult.
'The remedy is not to think harder but to consult the record' — the effective cure; remnant = a leftover piece.
'ignores the seductive details of the current plan' — deliberately disregards them; endorse = publicly support, entail = involve necessarily.
